findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. 

A food employee was observed to wash hands, use a paper towel to turn of the faucet and then use the same paper towel to dry their hands. The paper towel should have been discarded and another acquired for drying of the hands. Another option would have been to dry the hands and then turn off the water with the paper towel. Education took place and the PIC is instructed to ensure that proper hand washing procedures are utilized in the facility.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. 

The stand up three door cooler along the back wall of the facility is observed with containers of cottage cheese and chicken salad bearing date marks of 1/13/21. This makes today the 21st day since opening per the date. TCS foods should be used or discarded within 7 days of opening. PIC was consulted and the items discarded during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee did used their bare hand to turn off the faucet after washing hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Education took place.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

Observed a bag of sausage patties stored in the walk in cooler dated 4/26/18. This is now day 8 of the sausage's storage and they should have been used or discarded yesterday. While discussing this with the PIC the items were discarded during the inspection.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

Observed an employee retrieving a can of soda from the walk in cooler. Also observed a personal lunch stored in the cooler next to food intended for consumers. Personal foods should be stored separate from foods intended for consumers. Discussed with the person in charge and a tub will be designated for personal foods in the cooler.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed cooler holding potentially hazardous foods to be holding those foods at 50F. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) Foods for the salad bar including ham bits, eggs, cheese, salad dressings, individual soy milks were all dsicarded.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment: The unit showed a 5degree drop in temperatuer on the log over a day or two after being closed all night. Also the unit is said to come out of temperature quickly when the doors are open. Repiar or replace the cooler. The unit will be decomissioned starting today and the walk in cooler will be used. The unit is normally unplugged over the summer. 750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: No independent thermometer in the unit that is malfunctioning. 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F located in the warmest part of the cooler.  Provide thermometers for units

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: Observed wiping cloth buckets to be at zero parts per million of sanitizer. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.  Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510d Observed staff use freshly washed hands to turn off the faucet at the handsink. Cease recontaminating clean hands by touching soiled handle. Dry hands and use that barrier to turn off the faucets. Also, observed staff member to use gloved hands to handle pizza boxes and touch hair before returning to handle celery. Activity was halted and hands were washed with fresh gloves donned. To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door. 750-160bGloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1.Observed an absence of caulk in the dish machine area.  Caulk the piece of equipment to the wall.  2.Observed caulk that is cracked on the two part sink and three part sink wall. Re-caulk the sink to the wall.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
*Broken floor coving/baseboard tiles in the doorway of the dish room.  Repair coving tiles or place flexible coving over the broken tiles.
*Damaged floor tile in doorway to dish room.  Repair floor tile in this area.
*Loose floor coving/baseboard along the wall behind the chemical storage shelf by the walk-in freezer.  Replace the coving in this area.
*Soiled floor under the shelving in the dry storage room.  Clean the floor.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750.1200: Absence of coving/baseboard at the wall to floor juncture under the handsink in the kitchen and along the wall next to the handsink, by the entrance to the dishroom. In this doorway, there are also some broken floor tiles near the floor. Repair tiles or provide a baseboard over broken tiles and provide coving/baseboard along the wall to floor junctures that are missing it, or caulk the juncture so that it is easily cleanable and to prevent pests from entering.
